Title: Diagnosis of test `testReflectionObjectCycle`
Details: The test `testReflectionObjectCycle` checks the ability of `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode` method to handle cyclic references between objects without causing a stack overflow error. The test creates two objects `ReflectionTestCycleA` and `ReflectionTestCycleB` which link to each other, causing a cycle.

Both classes override `hashCode()` to call `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode(this)`. The failure of this test indicates that the current implementation of `reflectionHashCode` does not properly handle cyclic references, leading to infinite recursion and stack overflow.

The `reflectionHashCode(Object)` method delegates to `reflectionHashCode(int, int, Object, boolean, Class<?>, String[])`. This deeper method likely performs the reflection to compute hash code recursively on fields. If cyclic references are not managed, the recursion never ends.

The key to fixing this issue lies in the handling of cyclic references during reflection. Such handling typically involves maintaining a registry of visited objects during a hash code computation to avoid revisiting objects already processed. The test also checks that the registry is cleared (assertNull on `HashCodeBuilder.getRegistry()`).

To summarize, the bug happens because `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode`'s recursive reflection traverses cyclic object graphs without cycle detection, leading to infinite recursion and a StackOverflowError.

Next, I will check the implementation of `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode(int,int,Object,boolean,Class<?>,String[])` for cycle detection or registry usage.
